cards.title: Our plan came fourth
cards.text: Judges scored five unsigned designs against 32 real failures. Ours passed 7, the best one 16. Still, the final design came mostly from ours. Blind tests keep you honest.

cards.title: The checks we cut came back
cards.text: Ten days of research cost just 4% of the money and asked for three checks. We cut all three to go faster. Within nine days all three were back. Research is cheap, skipping it is not.

cards.title: Scripts beat instructions
cards.text: We told agents in messages how to wait. Their waiting still grew from 64% to 92% of their time. One wait script brought it down to 36%. Don't tell, script.

cards.title: Duplication by merger agent
cards.text: The integrator had exactly one job: merge. Instead it rebuilt one item itself, 66 files, no commit. The whole branch stood still for two hours.

cards.title: Record the agent, replay the code
cards.text: Live agent runs differ by noise alone. So we recorded the old agent answers and replayed them against the new code. Every difference left was a real code difference.

cards.title: From 8 to 3 agents
cards.text: On 4 Oct we added eight roles in 17 hours. Three weeks later the core was just three agents: one integrator, one worker and one reviewer. Simple won.

cards.title: The model wasn't the bottleneck
cards.text: The model ran only 26% of active agent time. Tests, waits and idle turns took the rest. Effort settings changed the cost, not the speed.

cards.title: Code history ledger
cards.text: Every past commit became a row with a verdict. With all tests green, that list still found 59 missing behaviours. Your history knows more than your tests.

cards.title: Predict, then score
cards.text: Each efficiency check made one change and predicted its gain. The next check scored it. One guess was off seven times, and only the score caught it.

cards.title: Cache busts
cards.text: The prompt cache lasts five minutes. Our wait script waited ten. So every call after such a pause paid for the whole context again: 3% of the calls, a third of the money.

cards.title: Tests locked by hash
cards.text: One agent wrote the tests, a hash froze them, another agent wrote the code. The lock caught six quiet edits to frozen tests.

cards.title: Communication delay
cards.text: An agent reads messages only between turns. Once merges got fast, a hold arrived after the push it was meant to stop.

cards.title: Review the whole branch
cards.text: Seven reviews of single items missed the two real bugs. Each bug crossed two items. Two reviews of the whole branch found both in 15 minutes.

cards.title: UI QA works!
cards.text: 47 CI gates had passed. 45 minutes of clicking through the app found five defects. You are still the best tester.

cards.title: Feature hallucination
cards.text: Agents added about 20 features the old code never had. Every check passed them, because checks test that a feature works, not that it should exist. We removed 11.

cards.title: Review as the bottleneck
cards.text: Agents wrote code faster than my peers could read it. Of 241 review comments, the first 81 found no bug, just names, placement and code nobody needed.

cards.title: 27 confident claims were wrong
cards.text: 27 agent claims were corrected later, "proven parity" among them. From 15 Oct on: no claim without a table of what its check compares against and what it cannot see.

cards.title: The whole team stopped 17 times
cards.text: Usage limits killed every agent at once, at least 17 times. State files kept all committed work, but old agents woke up and redid lanes.

cards.title: One gate set the pace
cards.text: Limits cut the team from 18 agents to 3. Commits per hour fell fivefold. We still passed about one gate per hour. The 3 landed what the 18 built.

cards.title: Freedom is per action
cards.text: I gave the team more freedom 8 times and took some back 5 times. Each time it was about one thing: pushing, posting or building before I decided. The lead treated every change as more or less freedom in general.

cards.title: 45 planned, 1,456 ran
cards.text: We planned about 45 agent runs. 1,456 agents ran. The forecast got the size of the code right. It got the way there completely wrong.
